body.p: Tablet to Translation (T2T) aims to advance the state of the art in machine reading of original clay manuscripts written in Sumerian cuneiform and machine translation of Sumerian. The initial phases of the project, funded with a generous three-year gift, will work on creating resources for machine translation (MT) as well as carrying out systematic testing and evaluation of modern MT approaches; another branch of our work will involve conservation, digitization, and sign-recognition experiments with the remaining unpublished Ur III administrative fragments currently held in the Penn Museum.
T2T owes much to previous work in corpus-building and computational analysis and will engage with other related efforts. Prior work is exemplified by publications such as the following:

ul.li: Shai Gordin, Aleksi Sahala et al., EvaCun 2025 Shared Task: Lemmatization and Token Prediction in Akkadian and Sumerian using LLMs

Bansal, Choudhary, et al.,
How Low is Too Low? A Computational Perspective on Extremely Low-Resource Languages

li.p: Gordin and Romach, The Cuneiform Wide Web: From Card Catalogues to Digital Assyriology
provides a useful synthesis of the various requirements and potentials of automated interpretation of cuneiform documents.

Punia, Shenk et al.,
Towards the First Machine Translation System for Sumerian Transliterations
Presents results from the Machine Translation and Automated Analysis of Cuneiform Languages project run by Émilie Pagé-Perron from 2017-2020 and based on the CDLI Ur III corpus.

Hamplová, Romach, et al.,
Cuneiform Stroke Recognition and Vectorization in 2D Images

body.p: We will work on building/improving translation resources in several ways:

li.p: Create a database of commodities and translations for the Ur III administrative corpus

There is an extensive secondary literature on matters such as age and sex designations of domesticated animals, technical terms associated with the production processes for wool, felt, ceramics, etc., dissertations on metal-working terminology, food, crops, and so on. This literature would be reviewed in order to provide translations of a list of commodities derived directly from the Ur III corpus: preliminary work suggest that there are approximately 5000 commodities that occur at least twice in the corpus.
Create a reference set of translations of court records, letters, and contracts
We will utilize existing published translations of these document types where possible and also translate additional texts.
Revise and update existing translations of Sumerian non-administrative texts

The ETCSL corpus created paragraph-oriented translations of the bulk of the Old Babylonian Sumerian corpus. These need to be updated and need to be revised so that translation units correspond to Sumerian sentences in order to support the creation of the CoNLL-O version of the corpus.
